text_fidelity_a:
Royal Medical Direct 180-Piece First Aid Kit - Hospital-Grade Emergency Medical Supplies for Traveling, Hiking, Camping, Home, or Auto - Portable, Lightweight and Travel Ready I am a firm believer in being prepared for emergencies, I have seen enough of them personally that I would rather be ready for it when it happens. When we were moving in this home, I stepped on a sharp object and ended up with stitches in the bottom of my foot. I didn't have a good first aid kit with me and we were scrambling around looking for something to hold things together while we went to the hospital. Luckily two of the people helping us move were doctors and handled the situation, but had they not been there I would not have had a good way to take care of things, as I was in shock and could not tell anyone where anything was. This emergency kit is perfect to keep on hand so you have everything that you need in case something does happen. There are lots of items stuffed in there and room to stick a few more items if you want. The biggest draw for me was the emergency blanket (going in to shock really does make you cold), the triangle bandage, the cpr mask, and the case is nice and rugged. I like having everything zipped into the case, I stuck a tube of neosporin and a packet of ibuprofen in there as well and now I feel prepared for just about anything.

*I RECEIVED THIS PRODUCT AT A DISCOUNTED PRICE (IN ORDER TO TRY IT AND REVIEW) THIS DOES NOT GUARANTEE A GOOD REVIEW, I AM HONEST AND UNBIASED, ALL OPINIONS ON IT ARE MY OWN AND BASED ON THE PRODUCT ITSELF.

SKLZ Pure Path Golf Swing Trainer Yellow, Large For anyone just learning the game of golf, like me, this SKLZ Pure Path Swing Trainer With Instant Feedback is wonderful. We have clay soil here in Ohio and it went into the ground really solid with a bit of pushing, then stepping down on it. I used my Taylor Made Burner Driver and all my irons every day for a week hitting the plastic ball and this trainer's spikes only had to be stepped down just a little bit once. It really doesn't move at all when it's pushed down in solid clay soil.

Being a new golfer, I have been learning to just hit the ball, focusing on my grip and how to swing. My husband takes me to putting greens and driving ranges- but when you just want to learn to make contact with the ball- it is quite expensive paying for those buckets at the driving ranges. I love this Swing Trainer, as it costs me nothing. You can set it up as you like, with three different ball heights, and being able to connect with the ball with your club coming up right under it, is just like the driving range.

The best part is, I don't have to chase after any plastic balls in the yard, I don't have to pay for buckets of balls, and that leaves me just time for concentrating on making contact with the ball. Not only that, but when you hit the ball, you can watch the yellow rope spin straight, to the right or to the left. I can actually see in which direction I'm hitting it. I know once I get my swing better, make good contact with the ball, feel my grip getting comfortable, and see most of my shots going straight, I'll be back on the driving range. But until then, I can practice making ball contact and see if I'm shooting the ball straight- right in my own back yard and the cost is nothing, which is just perfect for me.

Franklin Sports Kids Horseshoes Set - Soft Indoor + Outdoor Horseshoes Game Set for Kids - (4) Plastic Horseshoes, (2) Ground Stakes + (2) Plastic Indoor Stakes Included - Perfect Game for Kids This set comes with 2 blue rubber horseshoes, 2 green rubber horseshoes, 2 plastic ground stakes which can be pressed into soft soil (do not use a hammer!) and 2 free standing targets made up of a 1' wide rubber circle base, a weighted plastic stake, and a stake support base. The horseshoes are large (6.5" x 7.5")--much larger than a real horseshoe. You hold them by the top of the U and toss them at the stake. The instructions say that the stakes should be set up 10-15 feet from each other, with one team throwing from one side and the other team throwing from the other side. They suggest 4 people playing, but it works for 1-4 players. You score points if the horseshoe lands with the post inside the U (3 points) or the horseshoe touching the post (2 points) or a certain distance from the stake (1 point).

I initially used the 14" ground stakes pushed halfway into soft soil, and the stakes held well against horseshoes hitting them. The 6" free-standing stake is shorter, so a throw that might catch the ground stake and make a score might fly over the free-standing stake. I was surprised, but the free-standing stakes also took hits without falling over--probably because they're weighted and the wide circle base pulls them back down when hit. Anyway, the kids enjoyed this, though we started off much closer than 10' until they got a feel for the game. The free-standing stakes were easy to put together and take apart for storage. They do need to have dirt and grass brushed off before storage.
text_fidelity_b: Franklin Sports Kids Horseshoes Set - Soft Indoor + Outdoor Horseshoes Game Set for Kids - (4) Plastic Horseshoes, (2) Ground Stakes + (2) Plastic Indoor Stakes Included - Perfect Game for Kids

text_fidelity_a:
Alvada Merino Wool Hiking Socks Thermal Warm Crew Winter Boot Sock For Men & Women 3 Pairs Alvada says these hiking socks are 80% Merino wool. But the moment I put them on, my feet said "synthetic".

But I don't like to leave a negative review without reason. So, I did two tests:

First, I took a pair out for a hike on a drizzly day. Real wool regulates temperature in the "Goldilocks" zone: not too hot, not too cold. Real wool also wicks moisture. The Alvada socks were too warm when dry, too cold when wet, and they did nothing to wick the dampness away.

Second, I used a test that is familiar to anyone who works with fiber: the flame test. Take a piece of yarn and a lighter. When held to the flame, real wool will shrink away. It will burn in the flame, but it won't ignite or burn on its own. When it burns it smells like burnt hair, and it leaves a powdery ash. By contrast, synthetic fiber will not only burn, it will ignite and keep burning. Synthetic gives off a greasy smoke and leaves a ball of burnt plastic.

I posted a video of my flame test on yarn from these Alvada Hiking Socks compared to a strand of yarn from a pair of Darn Tough 68% Merino Wool Socks. Spoiler Alert! The Alvada yarn caught fire and burned vigorously. Totally consistent with synthetic material.

POTENTIAL SAFETY WARNING:

Metalworkers (welders, grinders, blacksmiths), glass artists, firefighters and others who may be exposed to flames, embers or sparks look for wool clothing BECAUSE of wool's relative safety. Synthetic fibers can ignite.

Dont get fleeced and don't get burned by synthetic socks posing as 80% Merino wool.
text_fidelity_b: Alvada Merino Wool Hiking Socks Thermal Warm Crew Winter Boot Sock For Men & Women 3 Pairs

Franklin Sports Professional Series Steel Ladder Ball I like the game, but there was a problem during the assembly. There are two goals with 3 colored rods that are screwed into the supports. The supports are uprights screwed into a base. Each upright slides over a projection on a base before they can be screwed together. Well, one goal assembled easily and quickly, but the other goal didn't. The projection on the base was too wide and we couldn't get the upright onto it until we used a power grinder to narrow the projection down. Also, one of the colored rods didn't want to screw on, though it can be done using force.

The game is for ages 6 and up. I don't know why this game is called a "golf toss" as there's nothing golf-related about it. It's a bolo toss. You hold one ball in your palm with the rest of the bolo hanging below, give an underhanded throw through the goal area, and get points if you get the bolo to wrap around a colored rod. The goals stayed upright without problem even when on uneven ground. I have no idea why they suggest placing the goals/players opposite each other and alternating throws as then you're throwing objects at your opposing players (unless you're really, really good at hitting the target).

We just put the goals side-by-side. There are 3 white bolos and 3 black bolos. They say each person has 4 throws per turn (yet don't explain why they only provided 3 bolos each). They also say adults should stand 25 ft away from the goal and kids 6-12 years old should stand 15 feet away. We've never done bolo toss before. At about 15 ft away with 6 tosses, I can usually get 2-3 tosses to wrap around the goal rods. At 25 ft., its 0 out of 6. The other players could only get points on 1 out of 6 tosses at 15 ft. Maybe we'll back up as we get better.

UPDATE 5/18/18: I've used this golf toss a fair amount, including using it as a game at a church "fair." No one was treating the game carefully, and it got a full days use. No problems with the bolos. The action of the bolos winding around the horizontals does slowly unscrew them, though, so we tighten the screws every few hours so the goal doesn't get too wobbly. People enjoy this game.
text_fidelity_b: Franklin Sports Professional Series Steel Ladder Ball

text_fidelity_a:
Pyle Sports PHRM26 Speed and Distance Heart Rate Watch with USB and 3D Walking/Running Sensor I had been afraid that the PHRM26 was going to be HUGE, like it looks in the pictures, but in actuality it is really quite reasonable in size. What seems like a 4"x3" face is more like 1¼"x1". Part of what makes it look so large is the black bump in the at the top of the watch. That bump is NOT mirrored on the bottom, and is actually INSIDE the band. What is inside the bump is a naked USB connector for plugging the watch into your computer. The connector fits into a little notch in the wristband to protect it, and the bump as actually much larger than it need be.

I had purchased the PHRM26 for it's ability to measure my heart rate. The instructions are a bit hard to follow, and there is no mention of how to activate the Heart Rate Monitor belt. APPARENTLY, you just put it on, and it works. No need to turn the belt off and on. (Makes no sense to me, the battery would last longer.)

I had a heck of a time getting the heart rate monitor to work because I was taking my cell phone with me, and it was interfering with the signal from the band. I didn't like the idea of having to leave it behind, but once I realized the problem, I used a Cell Phone Arm Band on my right arm, and kept the watch on the left arm, with my body between the two. After that it seemed to work perfectly.

Pyle Audio is a German company, and the manual is pretty poor translation into English, one that I doubt was done by a fluent English speaker. In fact, one of the most important parts of the manual was written by hand, is really in the wrong place in the manual, and gives a very slip-shod impression. Especially when you realize that the list price is well over $100! They could spend a little money and fix their manual.

Calling the included program disappointing would be an understatement of huge proportions, and is the reason why I don't give the PHRM26 a 5 star review. Oddly, it REQUIRES both a username AND password to use. In some ways this is neat, as multiple usernames allow people to SHARE the watch, as long as they exercise at different times. But the PASSWORDs can cause problems if, like me, you forget the password you used. I actually had to abandon my first username because I forgot it's password. Leaving me with an account I can neither use, nor delete. Once you get into the program itself, it's rather difficult to really make a lot of sense out of what it shows you, though it DOES allow you to both EXPORT and IMPORT CSV files that you can use in a spreadsheet program, which is nice. That allows you to keep your own records and manipulate the data in any way you see fit.

One pretty major drawback, is that the PHRM26 can only hold data for your most-recent exercise. Meaning if you forget to upload the data from the watch, the next time you exercise you will either delete the data from the previous exercise, OR you will ADD your current exercises to your last exercises, so when you finally upload the data, the current day will show the data for both days. So basically you need to upload your data every day.

The Pyle Audio (the manufacturer) website lists the PHRM26 at like $135 or something close. IMHO that is FAR above it's value. I see them regularly going for $45 - $75 in different places including Amazon, and IMHO that is STILL more than what it is worth. I was fortunate to find this one being sold by Amazon Warehouse Deals as an open package for about $25, and I feel that I paid just about the right amount for what I got. Now, the fact is that I'm a cheapskate, and I'm sure that there are many others who feel that it's worth much more, but the fact is that comparing the software that comes with the watch with the free exercise website LoseIt.com, and it's free Android app, the PHRM26 comes out very far on the low side of that comparison.
text_fidelity_b: Pyle Sports PHRM26 Speed and Distance Heart Rate Watch with USB and 3D Walking/Running Sensor

text_fidelity_a: GardePro E6 Trail Camera WiFi 24MP 1296P Game Camera with No Glow Night Vision Motion Activated Waterproof for Wildlife Deer Scouting Hunting or Property Security, Camo And this one I set up on my neighbor's porch pole so we had a cross section.  The camera I have had for about a year does fine for what I use it for - to see what critters come in my yard, but this one that I attached to my neighbor's porch pole...wow.  I mean the difference between the two is like night and day!  My old one takes okay pictures of the opossums and the smaller armadillos that can squeeze through the larger openings between my shed and the fence posts (not big, but big enough apparently), but my neighbor has heard lots of scratching around her home and so I thought this way she could see what was coming in her yard.  She doesn't have it fenced...anyway, this camera caught excellent stills of the huge armadillos (okay, compared to the bitty ones getting in my yard) coming into her yard.  They have huge claws and not sure if they are finding grubs around the edge of her house's foundation or what, but I think we figured out what's scratching around her house thanks to this camera!  My old one would have seen them as well, but the quality of the pictures just isn't there.  I'd recommend just about anyone interested in what critters may be coming in their yard at night try out this camera - you'd be surprised at what shows up!  For the price, it is SO worth it!

text_fidelity_a:
NZT1 M2 Night Vision Monocular I was a little bit skeptical of this thing when I first started looking at it. They advertise it more as a camer accessory than an actual night vision monocular. I decided to buy mine used as I am new to the night vision thing.

I love this thing! So here it is

Pros:
Solid
Functions as expected for generation 1
Comes with an illuminator
Great light gathering without the illuminator
Lens caps
Commonly used batteries cr123 for it and 9v for the unit
Carrying strap
Rubber eye piece
Huge objective lens around 80mm
Adjustable diopter
Adjustable objective
Long range 200yards on a crescent moon night without illuminator

Con's:
Heavy!!
Lots of focusing of the objective lens
Awkward to hold/the illuminator gets in the way a little
No actual on/off switch-just a button to push to charge the intensifier last about 2mins a push
Battery is awkward to put in

Overall this thing is awesome, especially for a beginner!

I paid less for it because it wasn't brand new, but it is well worth the money. I highly recommend this to new night vision users.

If you have been using other gens, this probably isn't for you.
text_fidelity_b: NZT1 M2 Night Vision Monocular

There are other pool alarms on the market which will tell you when the pool has been disturbed, but this system goes far beyond that letting you know about each swimmer.

Note that the band is about 14 inches around on the inside. But there is an included “extender” which will make it about 18 inches. So it’s good with not only small kids, but older kids as well. .. and possibly some adults.

I do have one “issue”. . . and that’s the cost. This is the one-band listing. Extra bands cost about one hundred fifty bucks. But if you look, you will see that currently there is a listing for a two-band set, which is even less expensive than the one-band set. . . and you get two bands. There’s also a four-band set, which can save you some money if you need that many bands. I’m just saying to check all the listings before purchasing. You’ll want bands not only for your own kids, but any visiting kids as well. I really think this system is going to save a lot of lives. You just have to make sure you use it each time you’re around water. It won’t work. . if you don’t use it.

text_fidelity_a: Master Sportsman Adult 26 Pocket Fishing Vest I have been looking for a vest for my camera equipment.  I got tired of lugging a camera bag around and having to set it down to use the camera.  I was looking at both this vest and the Uncle Milty Travel Vest.  Even though this is listed as a fishing vest I was leaning towards this over the other because of the price since they both had a 4.5 rating.  Because there questions on both vests about sizing I hadn't decided what to do.  Then a last minute deal came up for some travel I had to take.  I couldn't order a vest and get it in time.  I checked the web site for a Dicks Sporting Goods store close to where I live and they had vests in their fishing tackle department.  I went over and found a medium that fit just right.  I'm slender at 140# and 5-8 and have a hard time finding clothes over the internet.  I tried on a small that was more a juvenile size and not adult. The large was too roomy for me.  For people any larger than me a large size would work fine.  The funny thing is the vest I bought is the same exact same one here.  Mine says "Master Sportsman" and not Prestige but looks exactly like this picture.  It was the same price of 24.99.  I used it for my travel and several times since and it is really handy.  I've gotten away for SLRs and use a high end point and shoot camera: Canon PowerShot G12 and a Speedlite 270EXII.  Everything, including batteries and chargers and other stuff, fits in the vest just fine.  While the vest seems heavy when I first put it on I don't notice the weight wearing it.  It is so handy to reach in and get the camera, take some pictures and then slip the camera back in its pocket.  I'll never go back to a camera bag.  I have a small Eddie Bauer hand duffle that I use to carry the vest in.  I just fold the vest in half and roll it up and it fits in the handle duffle just fine.  Because of the weight I use a wooden hanger for the vest to store it on.  I hope the picture shows what everything look like.  It is a really great for around $25.  Enjoy!
text_fidelity_b: Master Sportsman Adult 26 Pocket Fishing Vest

text_fidelity_a:
Valor Fitness These squat stands are exactly what i was looking for. they are versatile enough to use with a bench or as a squat rack. They are very sturdy, although you need to have extra weight plates on the bottom pegs if you're doing really heavy weights.

I'm a 5'2" woman about 115 pounds so I dont have a huge amount of weights on these when I'm doing workouts. I think the most I've had is about 70lbs. But, one of the great features of these stands is that the adjustable height and anchor on the top allow me to also use these for chin ups! yep, I raise these up high enough so that I can put a low step underneath then jump up to a chin up position on the bar. I have my legs bent at the knees and crossed when I lower so I don't hit the floor. for the chin-ups I have about 40lbs of barbells on the bar and at least 30lbs on the bottom pegs of each stand and these are very sturdy.

I haven't actually used them for a bench press yet, just for squats and the chin-ups, but there is a safety bracket, plus a holder for the barbell when you're doing bench press. all of these are adjustable, too. When doing squats, the legs at the bottom have a thinner bar on one side that when you are ready to get the bar off the rack and step back, you don't have to worry about tripping over the bar at the bottom. Smart design. these guys were really thinking when they made these.

I wanted sturdy stands that were adjustable and could be easily moved if I needed more space. I probably could have gone with a slightly cheaper model, given that these are designed for 600lbs but I really like these stands and if one of my sons or my man decide to ever join me in working out, they can easily use these as well.

if you have a home gym and need something that will give you flexibility for space and plenty of options for your strength training, these are for you!

oh, and if you're a woman looking for a good weight program, I highly recommend [[ASIN:1583333398 The New Rules of Lifting for Women: Lift Like a Man, Look Like a Goddess]] - great program! (and don't for one minute think you're going to "bulk up" -- not gonna happen unless you've got tons of testosterone in you).
text_fidelity_b: Valor Fitness

Speedo Preflex Paddles These Speedo Preflex Paddles are designed to help competitive swimmers focus on initiating the catch at the fingertips in order to swim faster and more efficiently. The paddles are one size fits all, the they have adjustable rubber tubing that can be loosened or tighter to fit most hands. I have large hands for a woman and they fit fine. I don't know if they would fit or provide much benefit for someone with exceptionally large hands. I have used paddles in the past -- these are different in that the are scalloped around the point of entry, similar to how one's fingers would actually enter the water; they are perforated, letting some water through, and they are somewhat flexible with a high design in the middle, rather than being flat. The hinge purports to make the paddles beneficial for ALL strokes -- although I am ignorant of the science that supports that statement.

Overall, these are a great tool to change up your water workout and help improve your stroke. Give them a try.

text_fidelity_a:
EXERPEUTIC EXERWORK 2000i Bluetooth Folding Exercise Desk Bike with 24 Workout Programs and Free App Ordered in October and it is now February. 4 months of use. Sort of.
The exercise-work-bike took a total of 3 days to put together, and had I been doing it alone, I probably never would have gotten it. There is some form of blue “insta-glue” on the pedal screws that made them nearly impossible to screw in. 3 neighborhood kids and teenagers tried their best to help a lady out, but to no avail. Eventually, I hung my head in shame and begged the assistance of male-friend to demonstrate his masculinity and wield tools to get the pedal screwed in.
I am 5’8. That’s 68 inches or about 172cm.
The next issue came when I realized that even at the lowest adjustment, the one recommended for 5’1-5’4 heights, I still struggled to reach the pedals, sitting with my back comfortably against the backrest. If I scooched forward just enough that half my cheeks were off the front of the seat I could reach the pedals, the backrest, and still use the desk for my laptop! But the desk was still a bit high, so I used the tilt-a-table adjustment to relax my wrists and type with perfectly non-ergonomical T-Rex arms.
And now the clunking noise. I can’t stand it. It started off quiet, but after maybe 100 miles of use, it makes a clunking noise from the pedals and no matter how many times I tighten the bolts (almost to stripping them), the seat keeps wobbling and the handle bars offer very little support.

Overall, as a workout bike, it give options that a regular bike doesn’t have—a table.
As for the rest, I am very unhappy with the very little use I got out of it, the lack of structural support for a solid working/workout of cycling, and how fast it has started having issues.
text_fidelity_b: EXERPEUTIC EXERWORK 2000i Bluetooth Folding Exercise Desk Bike with 24 Workout Programs and Free App

text_fidelity_a: ELUTO Sea Deck Boat Flooring EVA Foam,Faux Teak Marine Mat Marine Carpet Non-Slip Self-Adhesive Flooring for Yacht Kayak Swimming Pool I'm not completely finished yet, but I purchased a used 6x12 foot utility trailer and built a Vardo or Gypsy-style camping, pull-behind trailer.  I wanted to do this build from the ground up as I have been teaching myself different skills, like putting together an emergency solar power station with a pair of solar panels, a 200AH lithium battery, a 2000watt inverter (with some other pieces) in a milk crate strapped to a dolly for easy moving - electricity goes off?  No problem!  But I have been looking into tying a system together for a camping trailer as well.  I mention this because I have investigated many choices people who do the nomading/boondocking thing and one gripe that comes up a lot is stepping into your RV/trailer.  You go to the beach, to the desert, to the mountains, to the lake and you will be dragging dirt, snow, water - all that stuff inside!  This boat flooring made perfect sense to me.  I lived aboard a houseboat and can affirm that if you spend time on a boat (just like an RV/trailer), you will be tracking dirt onto your decks.  So this is made tough to take all that and assist in cleaning the inevitable dirt and crud up without damaging the surface of this material.  I mean, think about alternatives - carpet, rugs, plain wood or faux wood flooring?  Plain wood might be sort of easier - sweep and mop, and it's cleaner, but once inside, do you really like the feel of that wood underfoot?  A bit of cushioning like this material has will feel better underfoot.  So, yes, I have installed this in my Vardo and I love the feeling underfoot. text_fidelity_a: Bicycle Handlebar, Lightweight Aluminum Mountain Bike Road Bicycle Fixed Gear Riser Bar Handlebar 20.5 inch Long Wide handlebars are good when you're in rough terrain because the extra leverage really helps. But in a more urban setting where there are smooth and level surfaces shorter handlebars work better. Particularly when you're sharing the road with the automobile; where just a few extra inches of separation might make all the difference to you! This handlebar also has an 80mm rise to give the rider a better, more upright posture. Everything transferred from the flatter bar to this new one even though it's about 100mm (4") less. I just came back from a long test ride and I didn't miss bending over to reach the flat bars at all... The control is better and since my head is more upright I can see better all around and be more aware in traffic or with pedestrians doing their unpredictable things. You need to know what sort of setup is the best for you, and it takes time to get that experience. I bought this bike new only a few days ago and the handlebars just weren't right. I could have looked a little harder for bars with more of a rise, but if I want this one higher I'll get a stem-riser headset and some spacers.

text_fidelity_a:
EVERCROSS Electric Scooter, 500W/350W Motor & 10" /8" Solid Tires, 20-22 Miles Range &19 Mph, 3 Speed Modes, Folding Commuter Electric Scooter for Adults Teenagers [[VIDEOID:7c963067c4b7ab3cf11ca74bdcaddaa3]] So my wife loves roller blading and after trying it a number of years back, we discover it is NOT my cup of tea. For all the things I can do, that is NOT one of them. So I miss out when she goes... and I started to see these eScooters and thought... why not? Had the chance to get one a couple of weeks ago, but then had the chance to get this EVERCROSS Electric Scooter and grabbed it. We like both - and now we can each have one for things other than her blading. Each has a couple "cons," but nothing we can't get over or around. And in the end, we really like them - both. But... I think I actually like this EVERCROSS Electric Scooter slightly more... here's our take:

1. It comes in a perfect box - meaning the packing and all was great for taking care of the EVERCROSS Electric Scooter while inside and throughout delivery. It is also great for gifting - the recipient will open it up to find... a fully put together scooter. The ONLY things you have to do: pull up and pop into place the front stick and handle bars and adjust the height of the handle bars. Both totally easy. There is literally NOTHING to assemble. You are only adjusting the handle bars to a comfortable height and it's totally easy. And you are popping that front stick with the handle bars because this thing is collapsable.

2. I repeat, it is collapsable. That means you can take it almost anywhere. If I had had this back in college... life would have been easier! You can literally break that front stick and bars down, and put them into the INCLUDED BAG that lets you carry this EVERCROSS Electric Scooter anywhere. Think about the student in your life! That huge campus! Or how about that "commute" in your city or town and then NOT wanting to leave the eScooter outside! This bag is well built, with solid materials and lets you take this thing anywhere! Oh where were you in college...

3 We got out there and tested - my wife on the first one, me on this EVERCROSS Electric Scooter. One of the reasons I do like this EVERCROSS Electric Scooter a little better is that i's weight limit is slightly higher that the other one. That means the weight I recently put on due to an illness does not keep me off of it until I get the weight back off - I'm out there now, not in a few weeks!

It is smooth, easy to ride, and you are up and going within minutes of getting it out of the box! The instructions feel a little intense - a lot to pick up and know, mostly around the box with all the information you're given while riding (mph, what level you are at, etc). I'm part of the way through, but I wanted to ride - so out we went. I can ride a SEGWAY with ease - when you get on this you'll understand that comparison - as this is about balance and the like. For we of GenX, (think skateboards and roller blades - neither I was great at) the SEGWAY was something I could master. So this eScooter I thought I was also in a good position to take on, and I was right. Balance is there, eases of use, turning, stopping... all there. Kids today... they'll rock this thing quickly.

4. Breaking. This is another point for the EVERCROSS Electric Scooter. The other one we have will stop on a dime! I mean, you hit the breaks and according to my wife, you STOP. That IS great for certain situations - and like this in reverse - you simply have to get used to it. (like driving a car). BUT, on the EVERCROSS Electric Scooter the breaks act more like a slowing device ... not a STOPPING one!
You hit them and SLOW down, NOT STOP. I like this from the standpoint that I feel as I have more OVERALL control as I am riding AND stopping. For me this is a plus. For someone else, they/you might prefer the STOP of that break system. My wife thinks she likes this slowing option better (and at some point we will be able to switch and she can use this while I try that), but for now, this is mine (maybe I won't take off that weight... ). Again, this slowing type stop means I can control the stop, the turns, and maneuvering while NOT stopping outright, but when I need to stop, I bring it down in speed, then you step off to stop. So far it has NOT been a problem and actually, again, I really like it.

5. There is a GREAT light! Do not let your wife, child, or anyone else "Test" it while you are looking directly into it!

6. There is an "emergency break" in that you can step on the back fender to STOP it - read the instructions. Apparently you DO NOT want to do this often or you'll wear out the tire.

7. The tires are great! I have ridden around our community and over bumps, "flat" speed bumps, those lines that are always painted with slick paint (motorcycle riders get it), and leaves and twigs... so far it's been great and I feel safe and in control. Fastest I've gone: 10 mph. We live in a community with kids and cars, so until I can get somewhere I can open it up... but so far so great and I'm having fun!

8. That weight thing... Check your weight and what it can handle. I did put on a few pounds and until I get those off and back to moving down, I cannot use the other eScooter. But this one I was fine within the limits. Which made me wonder, because this eScooter is actually slightly smaller overall. Including the wheels. So... why? No worries, I can still use this and it moves. I have gone up and down hills here in the area fine - we are NOT talking about LARGE hills, but enough that with my weight I should have noticed any issues and did not. It never felt like it was working any harder.

9. And once you get comfortable, there is a readout box on the handle bars you can track things like mph and the like. There are (I think my wife said) three speed levels - we quickly moved me up to #2. I am very comfortable at this level and should not take long to try out and use #3 - again, I am very comfortable on a SEGWAY, and again, this is important as the concept of balance and speed are very similar. The box is easy to read, though I've not even tried to change anything while riding and my wife being the one to read the instructions, made adjustments when we'd stop. I THINK this is how it is set up - to only adjust on a stop, but do not quote me on that. When making said adjustments, it's easy to use and to see. I am again, GenX with a need for reading glasses when... reading. BUT I did not need them to see perfectly fine and clearly the printouts on the box.

10. The handlebars... are good. This is another SLIGHT "con" in that they do "SHAKE" while you are riding. In order to fold up and then go down with the front stick in order to pack it away, they are bendable. HOWEVER, that means in the locked position there IS a noticeable shake or wobble to them. I REALLY noticed it at first and it did "shake my confidence," BUT I quickly got used to them and was fine. It is something my wife said, as she tried it, that it made her uncomfortable and it was one thing she put in the WIN column for the other eScooter. SO... it'll be a personal preference.

11. There is a kickstand to keep it up on its own. Well designed and easy to use!

12. SIZE MATTERS... Or does it?
We both agree the other eScooter IS bigger... platform, height, wheels, but... we also both agree, it doesn't much matter. I have put on that weight, I do not fit into the other one's weight limit, but I do on this smaller one... so.... does size matter? For weight, apparently not. FOR COMFORT... I did have to try a couple positions to decide how I felt I fit best on the PLATFORM. When standing you are likely not going to be standing front to back, but facing to one side or the other - this appears to be common on the eScooters we have seen. Okay, no worries... and I tried one direction (left) and was not at all comfortable. Flipped myself to the right and all was great! I fit - BUT I also notice I am in a smaller space than the other eScooter... but it honestly was not a problem for me. BUT a larger (read taller) person might find the shortness of the deck uncomfortable.

Overall, we LOVE this EVERCROSS Electric Scooter and are THRILLED to have it! Whether we take turns and switch off, this EVERCROSS Electric Scooter is a welcome addition for my wife and I. I'll be able to go with her when she blades or we can each take one and have time out. We have NOT had to recharge yet - we haven't been far enough yet to need it - so I cannot yet speak to that process. If it is anything but great, I'll come back to UPDATE. But we are expecting it to be as easy as the rest of our experience with this EVERCROSS Electric Scooter. In the end, would I pick one or the other?????? Ad of right now... yes, I think I would pick this EVERCROSS Electric Scooter over the other - for me. I 1. like the slowing of the breaks, 2. that it takes my weight - even when I loose it I like that idea, 3. that it fully and easily breaks down and goes into the included bag. BUT that does not mean the other eScooter does not have great elements to it. In the end... as far as THIS EVERCROSS Electric Scooter how do we like it? WE LOVE IT! This is a great eScooter for adults!
text_fidelity_b: EVERCROSS Electric Scooter, 500W/350W Motor & 10" /8" Solid Tires, 20-22 Miles Range &19 Mph, 3 Speed Modes, Folding Commuter Electric Scooter for Adults Teenagers

text_fidelity_a: KiZHXlo Night Vision Binoculars for Darkness. Infrared Night Vision Goggles for Hunting and Surveillance.Take Day or Night IR Photos & Video from 400m/1300ft. Our row of houses has a wooded area behind them that belongs to the US Army Corps of Engineers which is a part of the lake that isn't too far from our houses.  We have coyotes, armadillos, raccoons and a few more critters that regularly visit our yards.  My neighbor was thrilled to try these out after I'd had the first try - I did see a coyote pass by my chain link fence at the back of my yard and I'm pretty sure the odd things I saw were armadillos...hard to tell exactly because they are faster than you'd think, but considering the humped back, I'm almost positive the three I saw were armadillos...this works well for what I wanted to use it for.  My lot is not terribly deep and the government sends out a bush hog about once a month to keep the woods from crowding too close to our back fences so there is a somewhat "clean" band or swath of about 10 to 12 feet they clear.  Keeps the critters from taking over, I'd imagine.  Anyway, my next door neighbor is positive that she has had armadillos trying to dig around the edge of her foundation - maybe looking for grubs?  I don't really know, but that's what she borrowed them for - to see if she could catch them in the act.  I explained how to use them and did tell her that they use a bunch of batteries so if they went off, it might be that the batteries would need recharging.  She said she had a bunch of AA's - the next day she told me she did not catch one scratching around her foundation, but that she did see a couple run by on her side yard.  I told her she could keep them for a few days to keep and eye out on her nocturnal "guests."  These night vision binoculars are rather cool, though this is my first time using any so I don't have anything to compare them with.  For me, I think the price point seems high, but again, this is my first pair.  I can say that they work for what I'm using them for - it is interesting to watch the night time creatures that live behind my house.
text_fidelity_b: KiZHXlo Night Vision Binoculars for Darkness. Infrared Night Vision Goggles for Hunting and Surveillance.Take Day or Night IR Photos & Video from 400m/1300ft.

Champion Traps and Targets .22 Bullet Trap (Rimfire Only) I'd been wanting to teach my youngest daughter the basics of gun safety and help her get comfortable firing a weapon. However, I didn't want to take her to a gun range with its attendant loud noises and general confusion. I only wanted her to concentrate on the weapons and on what I had to tell her. We live in a neighborhood where the homes each sit on 2.5 acre lots--and most of them have surrounding fencing. While I could have set up a target range in our basement, I didn't want to deal with lead and gunpowder, and I also wanted to be able to push the boundaries to make her comfortable and capable with a rifle.

So I bought this trap and mounted it on two heavy duty pallets, put two more tall pallets behind it, and hung some heavy cardboard behind the target in the trap. Behind the pallets are some mounds of fill dirt and 100 feet of thick brush. In addition, there are no neighbors behind us for over two miles. The heavy cardboard was to stop any bullet splash back and also to help lower the sound of the bullet hitting the trap.

The final key to keeping all this a secret was to use two legal suppressors I have on the semi autos. You can use a variety of ammunition in both the rifle and pistol without having to deal with the "crack" of the bullets, giving you the opportunity to match each gun with the best ammo for it. And no one is the wiser. Mission accomplished!
text_fidelity_b: Champion Traps and Targets .22 Bullet Trap (Rimfire Only)

text_fidelity_a:
Avenir Dual Action Bell Talk about a good value. You can easily spend more, but I doubt you'd get a much better sounding bell. The Avenir Dual Action Bell has that instantly recognizable brrrriiiinngg sound that gently alerts people ahead that a bicycle is approaching.

It's not too loud and it's not too soft, it's just the right volume, and you can easily control the length of the brriiiinnggg, making it short or long. I have mine mounted on the left side, which lets me easily push the lever forward with my thumb. Again, the lever action is not too stiff or too loose, it's just right, allowing quick multiple rings if you like, but also giving excellent control for just a quick short half ring if that's what you prefer.

Quality seems quite high for such an inexpensive item. The attachment clamp (plastic) is nice in that it will close around small handlebars or larger size bars with it's long bolt. One point, be sure and watch out for the little screw at the top of the clamp (where the bolt screws into), as it can easily fall out and go missing while doing the attachment. It's VERY small and took me awhile to find, as it bounced quite a distance. All it takes is keeping your fingers on each side during the attachment process, not a big deal as long you know to do it.

Highly recommended for those who enjoy not only the wonderful sound of a traditional bicycle bell, but also getting a good value as well.
text_fidelity_b: Avenir Dual Action Bell

Solo Stove Campfire Camping Stove Portable Stove for Backpacking Outdoor Cooking Great Stainless Steel Camping Backpacking Stove Compact Wood Stove Design-No Batteries or Liquid Fuel Canisters Needed The third and largest in the all stainless Solo Stove line, the Campfire is perfect for replacing it's namesake traditional "campfire".
This past weekend I had a cookout with friends we had the Campfire and my friend had a propane grill.

While my friends grill was heating up, we quickly got a roaring file going in the Campfire. It was easy to set up and get going.
I keep a set of Fiskars pruning shears on hand to easily prep my stove fuel into about 4 inch length peices from downed tree limbs.

Start off with some small tinder in the bottom then a squirt of alcohol hand sanitizer as an accelerant, set it off with a lighter.

Begin adding on processed twigs from thinnest to thickest. I would say it was only about 5 minutes for the fire to get big enough
for the gassification effect to kick in and the blazing fire was eating the thicker branch peices with ease.

On this cold day we all enjyed standing around the Campfire to stay warm.

While my friend grilled burgers on his propane grill, we grilled onions and mushrooms in a veggie grilling basket on the Campfire.

We didn't want to fry the burgers in a pan and didnt want grill them over the Campfire because we didn't want to get grease all down in the Campfire.
When the fire burned out nothing was left but pure white as that was dumped out and mixed into the soil with a few good kicks.

The Campfire is too big as a backpacking stove, but is great for base camp stove or for backyard gathering.
When you want a campfire without a campfire ring and campfire mess, this is the ticket.

Highest quality product, highly recommended with no reservations!
text_fidelity_b: Solo Stove Campfire Camping Stove Portable Stove for Backpacking Outdoor Cooking Great Stainless Steel Camping Backpacking Stove Compact Wood Stove Design-No Batteries or Liquid Fuel Canisters Needed

It was impressive for the price. Stepping up to the alloy M was amazing. The phantom X impressed me enough that I ordered 2 alloy Ms ( one in the 6/1 the other in the 7/1 ratios ). I paired them both with falcon rods and 30lb braid. I've got older curado reels on all-star rods with mono line. These alloy Ms were easy to set up, I've never cast a buzz bait so far. The other rod was rigged with a fluke swim Jr and I could easily cast it to docks and structure. I fished a whole Saturday with only those 2 combos. I picked up the phantom x on the piscifun rod, man it felt heavy compared to the other 2. But it is a medium/heavy rod compared to the falcons medium. I've got 7 bait casting rods on the boat now, but I'll mainly be fishing these Ms with the falcon rods. I might in the future step up to the top tier reel, but these Ms throw the lure further than I've ever been able to with other equipment. Great little reels, just lube them up before going out with them.

(Update)
Both of these reels became very stiff to release to cast at the beginning of this year. One doesn't trip the release upon trying to crank back in. So I guess they are good for one to two seasons

text_fidelity_a:
Forgan of St. Andrews 21 Golf Ball Pick Up Tube [Misc.] This is a fairly simple product and, as such, you would think it would be pretty difficult to screw up. The theory behind item's construction is sound, but the construction is lousy. Specifically, I will point you to the cap at the top of the tube; this cap is poorly fitted to the tube and readily falls off w/o much prompting. There are only two things keeping balls inside this tube, the plastic claw at the bottom of the tube and the top cap. If one of these fails, you're left with an open tube that balls can fall out of at their leisure, which is exactly what I experienced. The top cap repeatedly fell off of my tube during use, a couple times from tipping the tube to where the balls pressed against the cap and a couple times after leaving the tube in my car filled with balls. I've owned other ball tubes and have been able to carry them horizontally and man-handle them fairly roughly w/o ever having this issue. The end result of owning this product that was supposed to keep me from having to bend over to pick up golf balls was that I was bending over to pick up balls that had fallen out of the tube. Sweet sweet irony!

I thought I may have just received a defective product and requested a refund from Amazon and was content to leave it at that. However, one of my golfing buddies said he purchased this tube and experienced the same issue, which leads me to believe this product is just generally poorly made.
text_fidelity_b: Forgan of St. Andrews 21 Golf Ball Pick Up Tube [Misc.]

text_fidelity_a: Ozark Trail 12-Person 3-Room Instant Cabin Tent with Screen Room (Orange) I literally looked at every single tent that was 4 stars or higher and slept at least 8 people or more.  We are 6 in our family but we always seem to have the neighbor kid wanting to stay over or my daughter's and son's friends.  So we tend potentially need room for at least 8 but would be better to have a 12 person as it gives room for more than 3 queen size mattresses.  We actually had 4 queens and a twin mattress in there.  Kids just had to roll from one to the other while we had little station areas setup in each room for the kids to have their laptops/ipads and even a small 32 inch tv.  Yeah I know it is not real raw camping it is in our backyard but still it is fun. Strung lights up along the way. Bought some 2 way radios for all of us to communicate while the kids and my teenage son stayed out in the tent.  We even have an extra Air conditioner we may use at some point if it is too hot in the tent.  I like the fact that it does not let water in.  The way the door area zips up it has a lower lip if you will that gets pulled upwards to create sort of a ledge that stands so the water cannot leak on the ground up into the tent.  If you keep all the windows and doors zipped, there are protective sheer pieces that zip up the windows, that keeps the water out as well.  We had a pretty bad rain/wind storm about 2 weeks ago. TiGr Mini+ Titanium Bike Locks. This Bicycle U Lock with Mounting Clip is Heavy Duty, Lightweight & High Security. Features Disc-Style U-Locks with 2 Keys (4"/102mm Wide, 8"/203mm Long) I commute by bike, and I have to carry my bike up and down a flight of stairs 5 days a week. My bike is an e-bike that weighs 50 lbs without any gear attached. After adding a rack, trunk bag, lights, etc., it's probably up to 60 lbs. The bike is fairly expensive, and I work on a university campus, so I need a lock I can rely on. I originally purchased the [[ASIN:B005VMO49U Abus Bordo GRANIT X Plus 6500/85cm (33.46 in) black - Folding lock, Bike lock, Security level 15]] because of it's high security rating. But it's SO HEAVY!!! It's almost 5 lbs., which means it adds 10% to the weight of my already very heavy bike. Hauling my bike PLUS that lock up and down the stairs was just too much.

Now I have this lock. I love this lock! It's so light! It barely adds any weight to bike. It's also easy to lock. I like that I can remove the barrel, position the lock, and then replace and lock the barrel without the key. The security rating on this isn't as high as the ABUS, but I see so few of these in the wild that I don't think your average bike thieves are prepared to break this lock. At least I hope not.

As an added bonus, my e-bike has a cage mount on it's battery, and that's where I've attached this lock. So when I remove the battery to charge it, this lock serves as a very welcome handle for the rather heavy battery. :)

As far as I know, no one's tried to break my lock yet, so I can't say for certain how secure it is. But it has a good rating, it feels secure, and it's light and easy to use. So I'm happy.

SecurityIng® Waterproof 3 Modes 600 Lumes Mini LED Bicyle Light Bright Headlight Lighting Lamp with 4.2V Rechargeable Battery Pack for Camping, Cycling, Riding It took a long time for me to find the right light on amazon, this one fit my criteria well.
1. this is compact
2. it doesn't have a huge battery that will get in the way.
3. It is bright. Im not positive about the 1200 Lumens, but it is as bright as my 900 lumen NR.
4. It is light weight. nothing like my other light,
5. I wanted an actual mount, not a rubber band.

I was skeptical about this light because of the following reasons:
-The name seems suspect. - not a name brand i recognized
- other reviews stated they had problems
-the mount looks super trashy and bulky

After getting the super mini light, I found it to be well made, and it came with a more compact mount than the one picture on amazon. if you go to the sucurityING website, the correct mount is shown. The light output is amazing. the light gives you a lot of down and side light, as well as distance lighting spot beam. it was well appreciated on the trail last night. It has a nice metal housing, and big button in back for high, low, and high-flash. which is really bright, and i don't see using that ever. The charger seems to be of low quality, but it works. my only ride so far has been an hour on high beam.

The only complaints i have are as follows:
1. the battery cable comes detached at the connector with vibration. I had to tie the connector together, and this problem was resolved. make sure you fasten these together, because there is nothing like going down a trail at night when your light goes out. luckily i was on a straight section of trail.
2. The mount takes a bit of getting used to, make sure it is really tight, otherwise it will move. it is hard to get real tight because of the weird mounting clip, vs screw. it worked though in the end. I would have preferred a twist tighten mount.

Overall, this is a great little light for the money. I am happy with my purchase, but cannot say anything about durability as of yet. i would recommend this and other SecurityING products.

text_fidelity_a:
POLAR V800 GPS Sports Watch/Running Watch with Heart Rate Monitor, Black This is the absolute worst training watch I have ever used and infuriates me to no end. Quick overview. I am a professional athlete, i train 6 days a week, usually twice a day. I take good care of my equipment. I rinse the watch after most workouts as directed. I do not swim with it. I do not sleep with it on. I do not wear it throughout the day. I use it for running, skiing, strength training. I am not hard on it, I do not throw it around. I have gone through 6 of these watches in less than 1 year. THEY ALMOST NEVER CONSISTENTLY SYNC VIA BLUETOOTH OR COMPUTER CABLE. I have a new iPhone 6S, and Macbook Pro. No issues with them at all, ever, except for f***ing syncing this watch.
Do not waste your money. The timer works great, the hr is great, the gps is great, the modes are awesome, the morning orthostatic test is awesome, I love everything about this watch. But the fact that it fails 19 times out of 20 tries whenever I try to sync it makes it utterly useless. I f***ing hate using this watch. Buy a Suunto or a Garmin. Just do it. Do not waste your money on this. You will get frustrated, you will get infuriated. I keep sending this watch back to be "fixed". Sometimes they try and fix it, other times I get a brand new watch in plastic. Literally. And then a week later it stops syncing.
Buy a Suunto or a Garmin. The syncing feature and flowsync software for this watch is awful and years behind the competitors. I bought a Garmin for back up and much prefer using it. My garmin (forerunner 610 used from ebay) never has an issue and syncs in about 10 seconds. It takes 5 minutes for the polar v800 to sync and it fails 19 times out of 20. Such a waste of time, especially if you're busy and spending 45 minutes of your evening swearing at your stupid polar watch that won't upload your workouts to your computer or phone.
DO NOT BUY THIS WATCH, WASTE OF MONEY, FOR THIS MONEY BUY A SUUNTO OR GARMIN!
You have been warned. If you buy this and end up pissed off waiting for the thing to work, then you'll remember reading this and knowing it was a waste of money.
text_fidelity_b: POLAR V800 GPS Sports Watch/Running Watch with Heart Rate Monitor, Black

As far as length goes, when I stand up in it and raise my arms straight over my head, there's still a little of the bag left over. (I'm 5'5".) It has a plastic guard, so that when zipping open/closed it keeps the fabric from getting caught up in it, which is appreciated. An air pillow is included with the bag and it's pretty cool. There's a pump built straight into the pillow. You can press it to air the pillow up. This way does take a little longer than using your breath(which is also an option), but it can allow you to get it tighter. You can add as much or as little air for your preferences, though. For lighter needs, we like this bag. We just wish it was a tiny bit wider.

text_fidelity_a: Bushnell G-Force 1300 ARC Laser Rangefinder I was looking to purchase a new unit for sometime.  My previous unit was a Bushnell from the early 90's, and it delivered faithful service for almost 20 years.  It finally died, so I began to look for a good replacement.  This product has a backlit feature that really helps in either bright, or low light situations.  On large objects, (A surrounding hillside) I was able to get it to range out to 1200+ yards repeatedly.  The compact size and power of this unit is a major step up from my 1st generation unit.  I will have to see as to long term durability, but the case housing feels solid, and it has survived a few outings into the High Desert summer time extreme temperatures (115'+).  It comes with a fairly useful carrying case with a magnetic closure, and a rather complicated carrying strap I found to be useless.  The directions are straight forward, and the ACR (Angle Range Compensation) feature does work,  is not TOO complicated and has been useful in my target shooting.  I do not give this product 5 stars because I have not had it long enough to determine it's long term durability.

While there are sometimes benches or natural features of the landscape that work well for meditation, this is not always (or usually) the case. I bought this hiking stool, to see if it would work well for this purpose.

I can happily report that for me, it works PERFECTLY for this task! I do not need back support while meditating, and for my height (5'6") I am able to sit on this stool with my legs at a comfortable roughly horizontal position to the ground. For a taller person, you may have to cross your legs, and they will not be horizontal to the ground, but that may be OK for you.

The stool is lightweight (I have no problem carrying it around for several hours, and there's a handy strap so it can just be slung over my shoulder) and presents no issues as a hiking companion. I did a nice sit with it yesterday for an hour in the woods at a park here in Baltimore. Lovely!

While there are a couple of inflatable zafu-style meditation pillows available on Amazon, I actually think for my purposes, this stool is superior. It will continue to come with me on hikes I intend to meditate during. I got mine on Prime Day, and I think it came to roughly five dollars with a ten dollar discount. Even if it had been about fifteen bucks at the standard price, it would be an excellent value.

text_fidelity_a:
Omron HJ-112 Digital Pocket Pedometer This is the 2nd pedometer I've owned. I bought this Omron to replace Walk 4 Life (W4L) unit I used for the prior 7 months. I was happy with the W4L pedometer except that the clip broke twice on it. And, because the clip is part of the basic W4L housing, you can't just purchase another clip - the unit is basically ruined (unless you want to risk carrying it loose in your pocket and opening it with your thumbnail). Therefore, since this Omron pedometer fits inside a separate hard plastic clip housing, I decided to try it.

It functions well, accurately tracks your steps, and has a nice memory feature to review the past week. However, it is close to 3 times the size of the W4L and, therefore, too bulky to wear under nice clothes. I was able to clip the W4L to my bra under a relatively tight fitting top, and it was undetectable; the Omron looks like a growth is projecting out of your chest. This seems to defeat the purpose of tracking all your steps if you can't (or choose not to) wear it, let's say, on a night you go dancing. In addition, although there's much less chance of the clip breaking, it's uncomfortable against bare skin and seems to me to be much bulkier than necessary.

In spite of these design flaws, it's a nice little unit for wearing around the house or in a casual/workout environment. In general, I've found pedometers to be a fantastic way to motivate individuals to just stay active, which is much more effective than exercise alone. If the only way pedometer manufacturers can prevent the clips from breaking is to make them as Omron has, it's far better than W4L's clip design.

If Omron could reduce the size of the unit, the bulkiness of the clip, and have the unit sit low in the clip housing (instead of half of it sticking up over the top), I'd give it 5 stars.
text_fidelity_b: Omron HJ-112 Digital Pocket Pedometer

Tungsten putty is important to get your car to maximum weight. I keep the unassembled car weighted at 4.9 ounces. I drill a shallow 1/4 hole under the car and pack in the tungsten putty to make up the last bit of weight. That way on race day you can make small weight adjustments without trashing your car. The fastest car is the heaviest.

I've been getting tungsten putty from the large online derby suppliers. I figured I'd save money in shipping, use Amazon prime, and try a new product. This putty is less dense than the putty I've worked with in the past. It seems to have more sticky binder and less tungsten powder than what I've used in the past. I ordered 3 units. They easily fit inside one container. I even mixed some tungsten powder to the 3 blobs of putty.

Midkawe Punching Bag with Stand for Adults & Kids, Adjustable Height Free Standing Boxing Reflex Bag, Ideal for MMA Reflex Speed Training, Fitness,Punching and Muscle Building Great purchase! Delivered with no damage and all parts accounted for. Assembly instructions were clear and easy to follow. They provided tools that will work but I used own. Easy to assemble, took less than 10 minutes. All the parts fit together easily, and seem very well made.

The base is very heavy when filled with water. It also has suction cups on the bottom that work very well on the smooth concrete surface of my garage. In fact too well. It makes moving it around a challenge, but on the plus side it dies not move at all no matter how hard I punch or kick it. Thinking about removing the suction cups because the base is so heavy when filled with water don't think it will move.

The spring is responsive and can handle some pretty hard hits or kicks without the shaft/bag hitting the floor. It's response time to return upright isn't too bad, just don't expect to rapid speed punch if you're going to really hit hard.

The red bag itself is super dense foam, not a leather covered inflatable bag as I've seen on others. It takes quite a pounding and it feels more natural than hitting a leather covered balloon. I've hit it without gloves no issues, but longer workouts need gloves.

The height is adjustable. I'm about 6ft tall, my son is about 5ft tall, and it easily accommodates our heights. A big plus. It's easy to adjust too, and locks in place very securely and stays locked throughout use.

Overall it is a great product and good value for what you pay. Well made, high quality feel that seems it will take a beating and last. Highly satisfied. Would recommend to a friend or family.

One suggestion: after assembly and initial couple of uses, retighten all the fasteners. Initial use may slightly loosen them. After the retighten they'll stay locked in place. I haven't had any issues with things loosening after the first couple of uses.

text_fidelity_a:
SHIMANO CS-6500 Ultegra Bicycle Cassette (9-Speed) I'm an intermediate level cyclist who recently moved to the Denver area. After nearly dying on a 2800 foot climb over 15 miles I noticed my riding buddy had about a gear and a half lower than me. I looked around and finally swapped my stock Ultegra 12/23 to this 12/27 on my 1998 Specialized Allez Sport with a triple crank (52-42-30).

After pricing the extra tools I needed to do a swap, it wasn't much more $ to just hand this cassette and a new chain to my local bike shop and have them do the work - still saved $50-$60 using my own parts. Since I have a triple, I also have a long derailleur, so besides the chain, there's nothing more needed for the swap except for adjusting the derailleur for the bigger sprocket. I think 27 is as big as I can go, BTW, given the range of teeth on my crank.

I haven't been back to that hill yet, but this cassette and new chain are doing fine so far. My second gear (running middle ring) is now like my first gear was. Given the 12T top end, I didn't give up any high gearing, but I do need to get used to the bigger jump between 5th and 6th gear (I think that's the spot).

My riding buddy has a double with an 11-speed cassette. I think we're pretty close on highest and lowest ratios now. Sorry, I don't recall what he's got. But its a fairly high end bike with 11x2.
text_fidelity_b: SHIMANO CS-6500 Ultegra Bicycle Cassette (9-Speed)
